Calculate variance of noise regions

Source: R/get_purity.R
get_noise_variance.Rd

Estimates the across-wavelength variance of spectral noise regions used in peak purity calculations.

Usage

get_noise_variance(
  x,
  noise_method = c("quantile", "threshold"),
  noise_quantile = 0.1,
  noise_window = NULL,
  noise_threshold = 0.005,
  lambdas
)

Arguments

x

A chromatogram in matrix format

noise_method

Either "quantile" or "threshold".

noise_quantile

Quantile of maximum absorbance below which timepoints are treated as noise.

noise_window

Optional range of row indices to use as the noise region. Takes precedence over noise_method.

noise_threshold

Threshold to define noise. Highest proportion of maximum absorbance. Used only when noise_method == "threshold".

lambdas

Wavelengths to include.

Value

Returns the average across-wavelength variance of the signal over the retention times treated as noise, or NA_real_ if no timepoints qualify.

Note

The variance is measured across wavelengths, not across time, since that is the quantity the purity threshold compares against the variance of each spectrum. It is therefore not directly comparable to the temporal noise estimate used by find_peaks and match_peaks, and the two diverge on data that has been smoothed along the wavelength axis by preprocess.
